![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/ac7f02919896aeb40859b1d78608ec7620c26ea77becc806a28d39ef8abacd12.png)

The region enclosed by the curves $x=y\operatorname{ln}⁡y$ and $x=2\operatorname{ln}⁡y$ for $y\in [1,2]$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=3.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
First, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/76196a70cdbc65d2f91b4ba500ea83083be5cfe10fe3f3bd09c035e3ea7bcfba.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x=2\operatorname{ln}⁡y,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $x=y\operatorname{ln}⁡y.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as a difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=y\operatorname{ln}⁡y.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/e5d8affefbde216fed0bf6acd7d464e921c1cf04e2578050d12c928d6dee5bd0.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}[\,(3)-(y\operatorname{ln}⁡y)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}{[3-y\operatorname{ln}⁡y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=2\operatorname{ln}⁡y.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/b4002c7922eac8e7c97d402833eabc3621ed4da2d13799d07206a45cf0afd1f1.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}[\,(3)-(2\operatorname{ln}⁡y)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}{[3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}{[3-y\operatorname{ln}⁡y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y-\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}{[3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}({[3-y\operatorname{ln}⁡y]}^{2}-{[3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡y]}^{2})\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
